definition: Semantic generalization is the carryover of meaning-based similarity between stimulus features, so that different features are treated as related because they share the same semantic content, such as “left” location and a shape pointing left. In this context, it can make effects appear to transfer across different perceptual dimensions even when low-level features differ.

reasons: The definition claims semantic generalization is “the carryover of meaning-based similarity” and that features are “treated as related because they share the same semantic content.” The packet only mentions that distractor dimensions can “overlap semantically” and that semantic generalization of stimulus features (e.g., left location vs. shape pointing left) may yield a between-dimension Gratton effect; it does not explicitly define semantic generalization as a “carryover of meaning-based similarity.”

The definition claims it can make effects appear to “transfer across different perceptual dimensions even when low-level features differ.” The packet states that semantic overlap between distractor dimensions may yield a between-dimension Gratton effect and raises doubts about generalized attentional conflict adaptation when semantically related dimensions are used, but it does not explicitly describe “low-level features” differing or that the transfer is due to low-level differences.
